text:
anna_cs: @devon_prod_engineer — ACME reported a 403 on both /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. They included repro steps and a note about token formatting. Can you take a look?

customer_acme: Repro steps: 1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' 2) Response: 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope"} 3) Token was issued by our provisioning script (bulk upload).

customer_acme: We inspected the JWT and see claim: "scopes": "inference|embeddings" — we used pipe delimiters on purpose because our internal tooling treats pipes as separators.

devon_prod_engineer: thanks. That explains it — our authz parser historically accepts spaces and commas, not pipes. If the token claims are literally "inference|embeddings" as a single string, the parser tries to match exact scope names and fails.

samir_infra: I can repro locally. Quick test: create token with header+payload where payload.scopes = "inference|embeddings" then call embeddings endpoint -> 403. If payload is ["inference","embeddings"] or "inference embeddings" it passes.

anna_cs: Can you add a short repro we can share with the customer and a temporary mitigation? They want a quick fix before rotating keys.

devon_prod_engineer: Temporary mitigations: 1) advise ACME to rotate tokens via the portal (portal normalizes scopes to spaces) 2) as a quicker workaround they can replace the pipe with a space client-side before sending the JWT to us (only possible if they control token generation). Neither is ideal for bulk provisioning.

samir_infra: Root cause: provisioner batch-upload script serialized scopes joined by a pipe char for legacy CSVs. Fixes: accept pipe as alias in parser and normalize to canonical space-separated string; add validation in provisioner UI; run a normalization pass for recently issued tokens.

svc-provisioner-bot: Incident note: batch-provision job #8423 flagged 47 tokens with nonstandard delimiter at 2024-11-16T09:12:00Z.

devon_prod_engineer: I'll open INF-3245 for the parser change (back-compat patch to accept `|` and `;` and normalize). Samir, can infra run a script to detect tokens in the DB with pipe-delimited scope claims? We should list impacted tenants and offer rotation assistance.

samir_infra: Yup — will run a scan against tokens-claims index, should be quick. I'll post results and a one-off re-issuer script that outputs new tokens with normalized claims.

anna_cs: Moving to customer comms: telling ACME we'll: 1) provide a short workaround, 2) prioritize a fix to accept pipes, 3) offer to reissue tokens if they'd rather not rotate themselves. ETA for patch?

samir_infra: Targeting staging PR tomorrow morning, canary to internal-sandbox in 24h, prod rollout 48–72h after canary if no regressions. I'll include a migration script to normalize existing tokens.

customer_acme: Appreciate the plan. We'll rotate keys in 2 hours as a stopgap and report back. Please share the reissue script if it finishes before then.

devon_prod_engineer: Action items: samir -> PR + scan + reissue script; devon -> INF-3245 + unit tests; anna -> customer comms + postmortem once resolved.

anna_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and ping once customer confirms rotation. :thumbsup:

samir_infra: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/patches/INF-3245 (draft) — adding tests for `|` and `;`. Will follow up with scan results soon.

customer_acme: Rotation completed, verified both endpoints succeed now. Will leave keys in rotation until patch lands. Thanks for the fast triage.

anna_cs: Closing loop for now, keeping INF-3245 open until prod rollout and token normalization job complete.
